A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ERMAR research. All five pages of v1 and eleven pages of v2 support comparison through readable text, equations, tables, and figures. v1 has no appendix; v2's appendix was included.

before.justification: v1 reports original ERMAR perplexity results on three language-modeling datasets and 4-shot/20-shot accuracy results on five NLU tasks in Tables 1–2.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds 32k-context evaluations, resource measurements, component ablations, and fine-grained context-length results, including Appendix A.4.

M1.justification: The relevance scoring, score-weighted TopK retrieval, memory pruning/update procedure, and objective remain unchanged. Newly specified BGE-M3, LoRA, and memory settings document the existing implementation; the added component ablations do not establish a revision to the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use SlimPajama for fine-tuning, PG19/Proof-pile/WikiText-103 for language modeling, and SST-2/MR/Subj/SST-5/MPQA for ICL. The additional evaluations vary context lengths and model configurations within this retained coverage, without introducing a new dataset, domain, or task.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in the matched perplexity and ICL tables, including MemLong and the RAG variant already present in v1. New resource comparisons reuse MemLong; BGE-versus-LLM experiments compare components within ERMAR rather than adding an external competing method.

E3.justification: v2 adds L40S-based 32k and resource evaluations, a standalone scaling experiment with 16K memory, and ablation configurations varying embedders, Flash/Eager attention, and context length. It also corrects the reported hidden dimension from 100 to 3200, explicitly identifying a typo. The original benchmark splits and metrics remain; these changes do not establish reruns of the retained tables.

E4.justification: v1 lacks component ablations. v2 Tables 7–8 examine embedder and attention/configuration sensitivity, while Table 9 tests the combined relevance/reranking mechanism with versus without that component. Table 6 and Appendix A.4 additionally investigate resource scaling and fine-grained context-length sensitivity.

E5.justification: v2 Table 5 introduces latency reporting with standard deviations, whereas v1 reports no uncertainty estimates. Neither version specifies repeated-run counts or seeds, and uncertainty reporting is not extended to the retained benchmark tables.

E6.justification: The original perplexity and ICL values are unchanged in v2 Tables 1 and 3. Substantial new results appear in Tables 2 and 4–9 and Figure 3. For example, the new 16k comparison reports lower reserved memory for ERMAR than MemLong (16.61 versus 23.77 GB), alongside higher latency (6862.98 versus 6496.00 ms).

T1.justification: Equation 1, the ranked-pair definition, objective, memory-update expression, and score-weighted retrieval formula retain their mathematical content. Display formatting changes and the new glossary restate existing definitions; no new theorem, proof, or derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: Both versions claim relevance-based memory ranking and adaptive retrieval improve long-context modeling and ICL. The introduction's three stated improvements and the conclusion are unchanged. The expanded abstract summarizes existing scalability and historical-usage claims, while new experiments support the retained contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of memory–latency trade-offs, embedder-dependent semantic performance, and context-dependent reranking benefits. It attributes the negative 32k WikiText ablation outcome to ranking overhead and PG19 benefits to nonsequential narrative references; Appendix A.4 contrasts factual and narrative context benefits. The original domain-tuning and noisy-environment limitations remain.

D1.justification: The new appendix substantially expands reproducibility information: tokenization, deduplication, stride/padding, training budget, learning rate and warmup, LoRA targets, frozen layers, BGE-M3 embeddings, TopK=8, memory grouping/capacity, and hardware. These are newly documented settings, rather than demonstrated changes to the retained experiments. The existing MemLong repository link is retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially expands positioning around external neural memory, retrieval-augmented generation, and neural ranking. Added works include Neural Turing Machines, Differentiable Neural Computers, RAG, FiD, REALM, DPR, ColBERT, and BERT reranking. The discussion explicitly connects retrieve-then-rerank research to ERMAR; the Borgeaud et al. citation is removed.

P1.justification: Related work is extensively rewritten into four thematic subsections, and experimental setup is reorganized and expanded into five subsections. v2 also revises the abstract, expands the author block, and introduces an organized implementation appendix and glossary. Much of the original introduction, method prose, and benchmark discussion remains.

P2.justification: v2 adds seven tables and the context-length plot in Figure 3. Existing Figures 1–2 are enlarged and relocated into areas spanning both columns, and dense inline mathematics becomes separated displays. The original benchmark tables retain their content, with the ICL table renumbered from 2 to 3.

improvement.justification: The added ablations and measured memory–latency trade-offs make claims that were weakly supported in v1 more assessable, while the appendix improves reproducibility. The net gain is limited by new reporting problems: Table 2 gives a 0.06% WikiText reduction although its values imply about 0.73%; the throughput discussion reverses the ordering in Tables 5–6; and Tables 2 and 9 give unreconciled 32k WikiText perplexities of 7.880 and 8.008.
